title: The control plane disappears
description: The load balancer's management service becomes unreachable. The L7 nodes still have a validated routing snapshot, valid certificates and working backend health checks. No emergency config revocation is pending. What should the data plane do while operators restore the control plane?

options.text: Clear routes so a disconnected node cannot serve an old configuration.
options.explanation: That turns a management outage into an outage for every application. A known-good snapshot is safer here than an empty data plane.

options.text: Keep serving the last known good snapshot, continue local health checks and alert on lost control-plane contact.
options.explanation: Fail-static behavior keeps existing traffic flowing without pretending config is still updating. Versioned snapshots let nodes catch up safely when contact returns.

options.text: Restart every proxy so it reconnects to the management service.
options.explanation: A restart does not repair the unreachable service and risks dropping established connections across the fleet.

options.text: Forward every host and path to the largest backend pool until config updates resume.
options.explanation: Ignoring routing rules sends requests to the wrong service. Availability is not useful if responses are incorrect or cross service boundaries.
